title: The Immune System
text: The immune system defends the body against pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, and parasites. It has two main branches: the innate immune system, which provides a rapid, non-specific response (e.g., skin barriers, white blood cells), and the adaptive immune system, which develops a targeted, long-lasting response involving antibodies and memory cells. Vaccines work by training the adaptive immune system to recognize a pathogen without causing disease.
